info.name: Purolator SOAP (EWS) — Production
info.description:
**Verified live 2026-10-06** -- every request in this collection succeeded (run in Development). Requests that failed or were not sent are not included.

Purolator EWS SOAP collection pointed at **https://webservices.purolator.com**.

EWS production host. Live shipments are created — use ValidateShipment first when in doubt.

Converted from the Purolator *Developer Test Aid 2.0.0* SoapUI project. Service paths and SOAPAction values come from the WSDLs cached inside that project.

**Before running:** set `SOAP_Key` (EWS key) and `SOAP_Password`.

Identical to the Development edition apart from the host.

*Note:* in the source project the Tracking and Locator interfaces were saved against the production host; here every service uses `{{soapBase}}` so the whole collection follows one tier.

---
### Environment required
Select the matching environment before running — every credential, account number and date resolves from it, not from collection or global variables:

`SOAP_Key` · `SOAP_Password` · `REST_ClientId` · `REST_Secret` · `REST_XApiKey` · `REST_Token` · `AccountNumber` · `Different_AccountNumber` · `Current_Date`

**Dates** — the collection pre-request script sets `Current_Date` to today. Create- and validate-shipment requests override it with **today + 5 days**.

**Labels** — create-shipment and document requests carry a post-response script that decodes any base64 label in the response and renders it in the **Visualize** tab (ZPL via Labelary, PNG and PDF inline). Set `USE_LABELARY = false` in that script to keep label data off the third-party renderer.

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}

// Writes the SAME environment variable(s) the REST request writes, from the
// first <ShipmentPIN><Value> in the SOAP response, so the SOAP document calls
// read the same names as the REST ones.

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.

// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.

// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).

// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.

// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.

// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

exec: // Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to

exec: // Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{#unless count}}
No ZPL, PNG or PDF label found in the response body.
{{/unless}}
// --- rasterise ZPL via Labelary, then render ---------------------------

// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather

// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather

// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.

// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.

// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.

// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.

// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.

// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

exec: // Create-shipment pre-request — shipment date is TODAY + 5 DAYS.
// Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation
body { font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 12px;

{{/unless}}

// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

REST description: French twin of “SEED · US · ZPL · Thermal · BASE64” — identical except the Language header, which is hard-coded to fr. A document's language is fixed when the SHIPMENT is created: the same PIN returns the same bytes whether /ship/v1/documents is called with en or fr, so French coverage needs its own create call. Captures into <var>_FR so the English seed's PIN is left intact. Seed shipment: U.S. lane, label ZPL / Thermal / BASE64. // Runs after the collection pre-request, so it overwrites the Current_Date
// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches
// --- collect candidate base64 strings from the response ---------------
// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.
// Postman's sandbox already defines CryptoJS as a global; redeclaring it
// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.
const zpls   = [];   // ZPL strings needing rasterisation

// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches

// Long, unbroken base64 runs — short matches are almost always ids.

// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.

// that script just set to today. Five days ahead keeps the date inside the
// carrier's future-dating window and off weekends-only edge cases.
// A run can override the offset with the variable shipDaysAhead (e.g. 0 = ship today);
// unset, it stays 5 days ahead (added 2026-10-06 for the production 2-key test).
// Carrier timezone, not the runner's -- see 9001-11.
// Post-response — render returned labels in Postman's Visualize tab.
// Purolator returns labels as base64. Depending on the requested output
// type the decoded bytes are ZPL (thermal), PNG, or PDF, so this script
// sniffs each candidate rather than assuming one shape, and it searches
// the whole response instead of hard-coding a field path (the field name
// differs between the SOAP and REST contracts).
// ZPL is rasterised through the public Labelary API. If you would rather
// not send label data to a third party, set USE_LABELARY = false below —
// the raw ZPL is still printed to the console.
// Rasterisation renders into Postman's Visualize tab, which Newman does
// not have -- and a pm.sendRequest() here REPLACES this request's entry in
// Newman's report, losing the response and its PIN. So it is on for
// interactive use and off whenever the runner sets DISABLE_LABELARY.
const DPMM = '8dpmm';        // 203 dpi. Use 12dpmm for 300 dpi printers.
const SIZE = '4x6';          // label size in inches

// with const is a SyntaxError there. Prefer the global, fall back to
// require() so the script also runs outside the sandbox.

// Collection pre-request — runs before every request in the collection.
// Refreshes Current_Date to TODAY and mints a unique RequestReference.
// Create-shipment requests override Current_Date with today + 5 days in
// their own pre-request script, which runs after this one.
// Two-digit padding for the RequestReference stamp below. Deleted by the
// timezone patch in 3be7aa3; every pre-request script in the collection
// threw `pad is not defined` until it was restored. Newman still SENDS a
// request whose pre-request script throws, so the run looks healthy while
// RequestReference silently keeps whatever stale value the environment
// held. Check the prerequest-scripts row of Newman's summary table, not
// just the assertions row. (The REST collections were fixed first; these
// three were missed and fixed a few days later.)
// Purolator validates the shipment date in ITS timezone. Using the
// runner's local date sends yesterday whenever the machine is west of
// Eastern late in the day, and the API rejects it (9001-11).
// REQ + YYYYMMDDHHMMSS, matching the convention used in the SOAP collections.
